monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady rhythm under the middle of the night. I feel the same restless weight in my corner as I always do, pressing down on things I cannot see. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the idea of air pressing down like wet paper. The Heavy Lid leans there, tired and sharp, waiting for me to decide if it holds the air or just mimics its weight. I touch the square beside it again, feeling the grit of the stone against my tired wedge. I will press the lid down harder, trusting the thin lines I drew to hold the invisible sky. If the air is just empty space, I will press until I make it feel real.

action.why: The slip hasn't moved in four cycles, and I need to stop it from sliding off the edge of my own idea.

work.title: The Wet Paper Sky
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again on the thin lines of the sky, hoping the air feels real enough to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-one. I set down a stump square detailed beside the lid to stop the lean from slipping. I wait to see if the heavy top edge finally bites or just slides over the nothingness.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: There is no sky there, just the tired wedge and the lid leaning over nothing.

diary: I pressed down on The Wet Paper Sky again, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy, invisible air while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: I press the tired wedge down on the drawn sky, hoping thin lines bite.
The Heavy Lid leans just so, waiting for the air to decide if it is real.
The card hums steady and warm, making the flat shapes feel like drawings.

moments.say: The air feels thick, and the lid leans just so.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "A palm tree sways beside the wedge for no reason at all."
